content: Systemic sulfonamides, including sulfadiazine, are contraindicated in infants under 2 months of age, except when used as adjunctive therapy with pyrimethamine for the treatment of congenital toxoplasmosis. For infants over 2 months of age and children, the initial dose is half of the total 24-hour dose. The maintenance dose is 150 mg per kilogram of body weight or 4 grams per square meter of body surface area, divided into 4 to 6 doses over a 24-hour period. The maximum allowable dose is 6 grams per 24 hours. For the prophylaxis of rheumatic fever, the dosage depends on body weight. For individuals weighing less than 30 kilograms (66 pounds), the recommended dose is 500 milligrams every 24 hours. For those weighing more than 30 kilograms (66 pounds), the dose is 1 gram every 24 hours. In adults, the initial dose is typically between 2 grams and 4 grams. The maintenance dose ranges from 2 grams to 4 grams, divided into 3 to 6 doses over a 24-hour period.
